title: Governed Python Service Platform
problemStatement: When the Knight Capital trading firm deployed a broken service to production in 2012, it lost four hundred and forty million dollars in forty-five minutes — not because the code was wrong, but because no one had governed the deployment, the rollback, or the environment. A service is not a script you ran once; it is a contract with operations. In this capstone you will turn prior logic into a production-style service with a versioned API, schema validation, authentication and authorisation, rate limits, secure configuration, dependency locks, a container image, non-root execution, health and readiness checks, resource limits, structured redacted logging, migrations, backup, recovery, security scanning, and contract and integration tests. A successful local demo is insufficient unless the service is reproducible in a clean environment.
intendedUsers: A platform operator deploying the service
A security reviewer auditing the container
jobsToBeDone: Run as a non-root container with probes
learningOutcomes: Design a versioned API with schema validation and authz.
Build a non-root container with health/readiness probes.
Integrate security scanning and contract tests.

syntheticDataContract.generator: Synthetic API clients and request fixtures
syntheticDataContract.schema: request_id, client_id, scope, endpoint, status, latency_ms, redacted_log

acceptanceCriteria: API is versioned and rejects invalid requests.
Rate limits are configured and effective.
Configuration is secure (no secrets in code).
Health and readiness probes are present.
Service reproduces in a clean environment.
criticalCriteria: No secrets in code or config.
Recovery drill restores service to a known state.

levels.description: All acceptance criteria pass on the canonical fixtures.
Core paths pass; minor edge cases fail with a clear reason.
Core paths fail or behave non-deterministically.
Malformed input quarantined; denominators correct; failures explained.
Failures handled but reasons are thin.
Failures crash the program or lose data.
Normal, boundary and failure tests present and passing.
Happy-path tests only, or boundary tests missing.
No meaningful tests, or tests fabricated.
Clear module boundaries; typed contracts; small functions.
Readable but with some coupling.
Monolithic, hard to extend or test.
Reproduces from a clean environment in one command.
Reproduces with manual steps.
Cannot reproduce outside the author's machine.
No secrets; synthetic data; least privilege; secure logging.
Minor gaps with documented remediation.
Exposed secret, real PII, or unsafe operation.
No unsupported inference; human review; correction mechanism.
Mostly responsible with one unclear claim.
Automated adverse decision or unsupported causal claim.
Inspectible traces, manifests, and lineage.
Some evidence present but incomplete.
No inspectible evidence.
Clear brief, demo and limitations; truthful CV narrative.
Demonstrable but with unclear framing.
No demo or misleading claims.
Criterion fully satisfied with inspectable evidence.
Criterion partially satisfied.
Criterion not satisfied.

criticalFailures: Use of real confidential, personal, employer-owned or regulated information.
Committed secret or credential in the repository or logs.
Unsafe SQL or unparameterised query that enables injection.
Public sensitive attachment or unredacted PII in outputs.
Automatic unsupported fraud, kinship, collusion, criminal-association, beneficial-ownership or causal-relationship inference.
Unapproved external side effect (email send, API call, file mutation).
Fabricated test evidence or a ledger substituted for execution evidence.
Inaccessible core workflow (no keyboard operation, colour-only encoding).
Unresolved critical security, privacy or responsible-use defect.
Final demonstration that cannot be reproduced from the artifact repo.
Local-only demo that cannot reproduce in a clean environment.

remediationPaths: If reproducibility fails: pin and lock everything
If authz is weak: add scopes and test them
If recovery is fragile: add a backup-restore drill
finalIntegrationInterfaces: Service platform → service subsystem of CP-FINAL
